items.title: Kpler/Baltic week: USG–UKC MR (TC14) falls 40% to $6.81/bbl; US Gulf Aframax (TD25) doubles to $17.51/bbl
items.summary: Kpler's weekly freight review, using Baltic Exchange assessments, has MR US Gulf–UK Continent (TC14) at $6.81/bbl, down $4.61 from $11.43 at the start of the week; TC2 UKC–USAC eased $0.27 to $3.44/bbl and TC11 Korea–Singapore fell $1.28 to $4.19/bbl. LR2 MEG–Japan (TC1) rose $0.83 to $26.58/bbl. On the dirty side, Aframax USG–UKC (TD25) roughly doubled to $17.51/bbl as US Gulf Aframax loadings hit a record 2.6 mb/d in November, while VLCC MEG–China (TD3C) held near $29.62/bbl.

items.title: Nortilus week 48: product tanker spot rates rebound roughly 9–30%; one-year VLCC at $165,000/day
items.summary: Nortilus' weekly update reports product tanker spot rates recovered by roughly 9–30% over the week and crude tanker rates by about 10%. One-year VLCC time-charter rates eased to $165,000/day. Listed product tanker shares rose 1.7% on the week but are down 15.8% month to date; crude tanker shares gained 4.7%.

items.title: BIMCO: clean-product cargo volumes down 11% year to date; tanker indices 25–30% off October peaks
items.summary: BIMCO's November outlook puts year-to-date crude and dirty-product volumes 5% below last year and clean-product volumes 11% lower. Middle East tanker exports reached 75% of pre-war levels over the past four weeks, while Russian clean-product exports have averaged 58% below last year since the start of Q3 after Ukrainian refinery strikes. The Platts global dirty and clean tanker indices are 25–30% below their October highs; BIMCO sets out 'Hormuz open' and 'Hormuz closed' scenarios for 2027–28 without numeric forecasts.

items.title: Diesel tanker that capsized off Ibiza: one crew member confirmed dead; no pollution reported so far
items.summary: gCaptain reports at least one crew member died after the diesel-laden tanker capsized and partly sank off Ibiza. Authorities had reported no pollution as of the latest update.

items.title: Hafnia defers decision on its $687m stake in Torm
items.summary: Hafnia has postponed a decision on what to do with its Torm shareholding, valued at about $687m, according to Splash. Torm previously rejected Hafnia's all-share merger proposals, and Hafnia had said with its Q3 results that it planned to distribute Torm shares as an extraordinary dividend; no new timetable was given in the headline report.

items.title: BIMCO issues tanker clause putting STS transfer costs and risks on charterers
items.summary: BIMCO has published a standard clause for tanker charter parties covering ship-to-ship transfers and special operations. It assigns the related costs and risks to charterers while preserving the master's authority over vessel safety.

items.title: EU's 22nd Russia sanctions package, including a ban on Russian-insured tankers, held up by Bulgaria
items.summary: The European Commission's proposed 22nd package would bar tankers insured in Russia and repair services at Russian refineries. The Kyiv Independent reports Bulgaria is withholding its approval in an effort to secure concessions; no adoption date has been set.

items.title: CENTCOM: US aircraft disabled Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in Gulf of Oman on Nov 26; six ships disabled since July
items.summary: US Central Command said an American aircraft struck the stern of the Pacific Archer, which had left Bandar Abbas, after it ignored repeated warnings while trying to run the blockade; propulsion was disabled and the crew was unharmed. CENTCOM counts six ships disabled and 158 redirected since the blockade resumed in July. Separately, the IRGC claimed one of two tankers attempting a Hormuz transit on Friday hit a mine — this is unverified.

items.title: Vortexa: Hormuz tanker traffic rose in November even as attacks on ships increased
items.summary: Vortexa tracking data cited by gCaptain show tanker transits of the Strait of Hormuz climbed this month despite a rise in attacks on vessels; Splash247 separately counts 17 tanker strikes in the area so far in November.

items.title: Jazan refinery strike kills one worker; coalition says it hit 50 Houthi targets
items.summary: A strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Nov 26 killed a Nepali worker, injured others and caused a fire and temporary shutdown of some operations, according to the Saudi energy ministry; the Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis. The coalition said it then destroyed 50 targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada, including the launcher used in the attack.

items.title: Abu Dhabi restricts tanker movements over Gulf security
items.summary: Abu Dhabi authorities have placed restrictions on tanker movements in response to rising security risks in Gulf waters. ADNOC also confirmed that a Jordanian crew member missing since the Nov 17 attack on an ADNOC L&S vessel in Hormuz was found dead; two of 11 injured crew remain in care.

items.title: UNCTAD: seaborne trade flat in 2026; IMO confirms 141 attacks in Hormuz region
items.summary: UNCTAD's Review of Maritime Transport 2026 says global maritime trade stalled this year after 1.9% growth in 2025 to 12.3bn tonnes. The IMO has confirmed 141 attacks across Hormuz and the wider Middle East as of Nov 23, with 25 seafarer deaths; late-November Hormuz traffic averaged about 4–28 ships a day against 85–140 before the war. UKMTO logged about 22 incidents in November, 10 involving tankers.

items.title: Containership sinks off Cuba; one seafarer dead, three missing
items.summary: Splash247 reports a boxship sank off Cuba, leaving one crew member dead and three missing. Vessel details and cause were not available in the listing reviewed.

items.title: Lower Mississippi at New Orleans: Coast Guard safety zone remains through Dec 11
items.summary: The Coast Guard's safety zone for the salvage of a river cruise ship after its collision with a tanker near New Orleans remains in place through Dec 11, with traffic restrictions on that stretch of the river.

items.title: Close Fri Nov 27 (half day): S&P 500 7,297.49 (+1.60%), Dow 50,774.94 (+1.18%), Nasdaq 24,129.50 (+2.31%)
items.summary: In the holiday-shortened session (stocks closed 1 p.m. ET) the S&P 500 rose 114.71 points, the Dow 591.99 and the Nasdaq 543.70, led by a rebound in technology and chip shares (PHLX Semiconductor index +4.69%); all 11 S&P sectors gained on thin volume. For the week the S&P 500 rose 5.6%, the Dow 5.5% and the Nasdaq 6.7%, though recaps note November remains a down month.

items.title: Oil Friday: WTI settles $83.08 (−0.72%), Brent January $95.44 (+0.88%); US natural gas +6.8% to $3.491
items.summary: Capp Notes' closing recap gives WTI at $83.08 and Brent at $95.44 for Friday, with WTI posting a fourth weekly loss; other recaps show differing figures for the thin holiday trade, so treat these as provisional. US natural gas futures rose 6.79% to $3.491/MMBtu. OPEC+ meets Sunday, Nov 29, and Reuters reported output targets are expected to stay unchanged through at least Q1 2027, an agreement described as in principle, not final.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield 4.94% (+9 bp); markets price near-certain 25 bp Fed hike at Dec 8–9 meeting
items.summary: Treasury yields rose Friday, with the 10-year at about 4.94%, the 2-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.33%. CME FedWatch showed 97.4% odds of a quarter-point rate increase at the Dec 8–9 FOMC meeting after a firmer-than-expected core PCE reading this week; the November jobs report is due next Friday.

items.title: Dollar index 104.04 (+0.36%); yen at 159.55; Brazil's real gains about 4% on finance minister pick
items.summary: The dollar index ended near 104.04 after touching a 22-month high of 104.53 earlier in the week; EUR/USD was 1.0939 and USD/JPY 159.55. USD/BRL fell 3.97% to 5.5156 after President Lula named Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco as finance minister. Gold futures rose 3.75% to $3,668.50, silver 9.11% to $43.70 and copper 5.03% to $5.60/lb.

items.title: Deals and data: Targa in talks to buy Kinetik; US October goods trade deficit widens to $149.5bn
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Targa Resources is in talks to acquire midstream operator Kinetik, with a deal possible as soon as next week; Kinetik shares rose 9.25% and Targa's fell 1.74%. The US advance goods trade deficit for October widened 10.7% to $149.5 billion, above the $133 billion consensus, as imports rose $21.1 billion.

items.title: Asia and Europe Friday: Kospi +4.34%, Shanghai +3.73%, Nikkei +2.11%; Stoxx 600 +1.08%
items.summary: Asian markets rose after Beijing pledged support for equities: the Nikkei 225 closed at 58,711.11, the Hang Seng at 22,694.77 (+2.11%), the Shanghai Composite at 3,606.49 and the Kospi at 4,915.68, while India's Nifty 50 fell 1.07%. Europe's Stoxx 600 gained 1.08% to 643.85.

items.title: Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if US conditions are met, including lifting the blockade
items.summary: Euronews reports the Iranian side has said the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within two days if its demands — among them an end to the US naval blockade — are accepted.

items.title: Drone attack in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians; Iran denies role and offers joint probe
items.summary: A drone struck an air-defence system in Kuwait, injuring four people; two Italians working for Rheinmetall Italia later died. Iran's military denied involvement and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offered a joint investigation with Kuwait and Italy. Saudi Arabia and the UK condemned the attack, and EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for more pressure on Iran.

items.title: Russia launches 162 drones overnight as Ukraine marks Holodomor Remembrance Day
items.summary: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 162 drones from the evening of Nov 27, 74 of them jet-powered, and that 141 were shot down or suppressed; impacts were recorded at 13 locations. Officials report the toll in Nizhyn rose to three dead and seven injured. Figures are from Ukrainian official sources compiled in a secondary summary.

items.title: Ukraine halts electricity exports as Russian strikes strain the power grid
items.summary: Ukraine has stopped exporting electricity as repeated Russian attacks on energy infrastructure strain its grid; Russian strikes over the previous day killed six people and injured 25, with outages in six regions.

items.title: Trump adds Ukraine to a warning against widening the war, departing from a joint NATO statement
items.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports President Trump's statement cautioning against expanding the conflict also named Ukraine, a difference from the wording of the joint NATO statement.

items.title: EU budget summit ends without agreement
items.summary: An EU leaders' summit on the bloc's budget broke up without a deal on Nov 27, with leaders holding to their positions, Euronews reports. Spain holds a general election on Sunday, Nov 29.

items.title: Bundestag approves record 2027 budget with €210bn borrowing, including nearly €12bn for Ukraine
items.summary: German lawmakers passed the 2027 federal budget with record net borrowing of €210 billion. The plan includes close to €12 billion in support for Ukraine.

items.title: Steelers 27, Broncos 5: Denver falls to 8–3; next vs Dolphins Sun Dec 6, 3:05 pm CT
items.summary: Pittsburgh scored two defensive touchdowns — a fumble recovery in the end zone and a Jalen Ramsey interception return — and led 24–5 at halftime. Bo Nix went 22 of 40 for 169 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble. At 8–3, SB Nation says Denver still leads Kansas City in the AFC West on a common-opponents tiebreaker; ESPN notes Denver is two games behind Buffalo for the AFC's top seed.

items.title: Texans (4–6) host Ravens (4–7) Sunday at noon CT on CBS; Hunter questionable
items.summary: Houston hosts Baltimore on Nov 29; the Ravens arrive on a six-game losing streak and, per AP, without Lamar Jackson. On ESPN's injury report Danielle Hunter (hamstring), Dalton Schultz (illness), Kayshon Boutte (hip), Sheldon Rankins (ankle) and Woody Marks (concussion) are questionable for Houston; Derrick Henry (concussion) is questionable for Baltimore. The Texans then play at Pittsburgh on Dec 6 at 7:20 pm CT.

items.title: Davis Cup: defending champion Italy beats Czechia to reach a fourth straight final
items.summary: Italy defeated Czechia in Friday's semifinal in Bologna to advance to Sunday's championship tie; Lorenzo Musetti had won the opening rubber over Jakub Mensik 6-3, 6-4. Full rubber scores were not available in the sources checked.

items.title: Davis Cup semifinal: Great Britain vs Spain today; final Sunday Nov 29 at 8 am CT
items.summary: Great Britain, in its first semifinal in seven years, plays Spain (without Carlos Alcaraz) in Bologna on Saturday from 11:00 GMT (5 am CT). The winner meets Italy in Sunday's final at 3 pm CET (8 am CT).
